rulers.name: Heraclius II (Erekle II)
rulers.note: Succeeded his father Teimuraz II as king of Kartli in 1762 (the Kartli page footnote gives Teimuraz II 1732-44 in Kakheti and 1744-62 in Kartli); died on 14 January 1798 in the text, 11 January in the table.

rulers.name: George XII
rulers.note: Reign 'from January 11, 1798' to 28 December 1800; 'King George had died ... before learning that he had lost his throne'. The tsar's decree of 18 December 1800 deposed the Bagratids.

correction.text: Kartli and Kakheti united under Heraclius II in 1762

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the founding year: Cliopatria draws Kartli (its Kingdom of Georgia row, 31,452 km2) and Kakheti (its Kingdom of Kakheti row, 23,396 km2) as two states in 1762, but the page says the kingdom 'was created in 1762 by the unification of the two eastern Georgian kingdoms of Kartli and Kakheti'; the union is drawn from the first year.

55.3 k km2 against 31.5 k (Kartli) plus 23.4 k (Kakheti) = 54.8 k in 1762, a +0.9% difference. The page gives no area and no description of the frontier ('Extent of the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti' is a map caption); it names no frontier and no vassal khanates of Heraclius: the 'subordinate khans of Erivan and Ganja' on the page are Agha Mohammad Khan's ('he gathered more support from his subordinate khans of Erivan and Ganja'), and Karabakh appears only as the khanate he had just taken. [Reviewer eu-19-d, 2026-10-31: misattribution corrected.]

54.8 k km2, a -0.9% change at 1775 that no page dates or explains (Cliopatria cell noise). Unchanged by the Treaty of Georgievsk of 24 July 1783, which 'guaranteed its territorial integrity' without defining a border (Georgievsk page).

54.9 k km2 for the single year 1796, the year after the Qajar sack of Tbilisi. The Krtsanisi page speaks of 'the temporary absorption of eastern Georgia into the Iranian empire' and of Heraclius returning to Tbilisi 'to rebuild the city', with no date for either; the kingdom is kept whole.
54.8 k km2. Agha Mohammad Shah was assassinated in 1797 'while preparing a second expedition against Georgia'; the page records no territorial change.

correction.text: the same outline, but ending in 1801

keyframe_review.note: 54.8 k km2, drawn to 1802. The kingdom ends in 1801: the tsar 'issued a decree on December 18, 1800 annexing Kartli-Kakheti to Russia', Alexander I 'proceeded to confirm annexation' on 12 September 1801, and 'By the following April, Russian troops took control of the country's administration'. The outline is right; the years should stop at 1801.

region.text: the eastern Georgian kingdoms of Kartli and Kakheti

ledger.note: 1762: Heraclius II unites Kartli and Kakheti. The kingdom 'was created in 1762 by the unification of the two eastern Georgian kingdoms of Kartli and Kakheti'; Kartli page: 'After Teimuraz II's death in 1762, Irakli II assumed control over Kartli'. The page gives no month; capital Tbilisi.

1762: Kakheti is absorbed into the united kingdom ('the unification of the two eastern Georgian kingdoms'); the Kartli page footnote has Teimuraz II ruling Kakheti 1732-44 and Kartli 1744-62, and the union page names no earlier Kakheti king for Heraclius.

8 September 1795: Agha Mohammad Khan fights for Tbilisi. He crossed the Aras in August with 70,000 men, forced the khans of Ganja and Erivan into alliance and the Karabakh khan to surrender; the Battle of Krtsanisi was fought 'from September 8 to September 11, 1795' and Tbilisi was 'completely sacked' on the 11th. Russia, bound by the Treaty of Georgievsk, 'did nothing to help'.

Late September 1795: the Qajar army leaves. 'The Persian army marched back laden with spoil and carrying off some 15,000 captives'; 'Agha Muhammad Khan remained nine days in the vicinity of Tiflis'. The page gives no exact date for the withdrawal; it also speaks of 'the temporary absorption of eastern Georgia into the Iranian empire'.

12 September 1801: Russia annexes Kartli-Kakheti. Paul I 'issued a decree on December 18, 1800 annexing Kartli-Kakheti to Russia and deposing the Bagratids'; 'on September 12, 1801, Alexander proceeded to confirm annexation'; 'By the following April, Russian troops took control of the country's administration'. Cliopatria draws the kingdom to 1802.

wars.name: Qajar invasion of Georgia
wars.outcome: Qajar victory at Krtsanisi (8-11 September 1795): 'The Georgians had lost 4,000 men in the battle, the Iranians 13,000'; Tbilisi was sacked and some 15,000 captives taken. No annexation followed; Russia declared war on Persia in 1796 and Zubov's army was recalled by Paul I in November.
wars.note: The khans of Ganja and Erivan were forced into alliance with Persia.

certainty.note: No page gives a frontier: the Treaty of Georgievsk (24 July 1783) 'guaranteed its territorial integrity' without defining the borders, and no page opened names any khanate as tributary to the kingdom (the Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti page calls the khans of Erivan and Ganja Agha Mohammad Khan's 'subordinate khans'), so none is drawn.

notes: Split-off from Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Georgia' row (39 shapes, 1010..1802): this dossier reviews only the five shapes 1763..1802 and adds a 1762 keyframe; the united Kingdom of Georgia (1008-1478) is kingdom-of-georgia, written in the same batch, and the Kartli years are in kingdom-of-kartli. Slug from tools/slug.py slugify('Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti'); the Wikidata id is unknown to the agent (Wikidata is unreachable), so identity.wikidata is null; Cliopatria's Q154667 belongs to the whole row. The kingdom-of-kartli and kingdom-of-kakheti dossiers list kingdom-of-georgia as their 1762 successor; it should be kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti. Russia's protectorate over the kingdom from the Treaty of Georgievsk (signed 24 July 1783, ratified in 1784 by Heraclius II and Catherine) is a vassal relation that belongs to the russian-empire dossier (vassal_start 1783-07, counterpart kingdom-of-kartli-kakheti; vassal_end 1801-09 at the annexation); Persia's brief 1795 'absorption' of eastern Georgia belongs to qajar-dynasty. Pages: Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti, Treaty of Georgievsk, Battle of Krtsanisi, Kingdom of Kartli (4 pages). Page silences: no area, no frontier, no list of vassal khanates; the Georgievsk page says nothing on Russian troops 1783-1787 or the Russo-Turkish war of 1787-1792; the 1799 stationing of Russian troops is a single sentence ('In the same year Russian troops were stationed in Kartli-Kakheti'). Conflicts between pages: George XII's accession is 11 January 1798 in the table and 14 January in the text; the annexation is dated 18 December 1800 (decree) or 12 September 1801 (confirmation). Counterpart dossiers needed: qajar-dynasty exists (me-10); the khanates of Ganja, Erivan and Karabakh sit in khanates-of-the-caucasus (eu-19).
